note: Do Mi Sol goes from a bare drill over a drone (3 minutes, the cap) to a tune that skips, then to the chord notes over a backing track, so the longer singing time is musical. The old Key selector is now moves (any key), so no selector is named and no chord is named by its letter: the backing track's chords are "the 1 chord" and "the 5 chord", and the staff follows their roots. The skip up to Sol carries the one care line, and every high note is on "oo".

exercise.title: Do Mi Sol: skip, sing a tune, sing over chords
exercise.why: Do, Mi and Sol are the three notes of the home chord, so the same skips come back in tune after tune: learn how they sound once and you can sing them in any key.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff, the five lines of music. Start on a {{1}} that sits easily in your voice and sing {{1}}, {{3}}, {{5}}, then back down. Sing it on the note names.
Then skip straight from {{1}} to {{5}} and back, and hold each note until your line settles on it.
_Don't reach for high notes: start from the low {{1}} when the high one feels tight._
In another key the drone and the notes move, and the skips still sound the same.

Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then press Play again and sing along. Sing it on "oo".
Once you can hum the tune before it plays, sing it first, then press Play to check it against the tune.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, the 1 chord and the 5 chord taking turns, one bar each. Sing the ringed note over each chord: {{1}} over the 1 chord, {{5}} over the 5 chord. Sing it on "oo".
If you come in late, hold your note and catch the next change.
Then sing {{3}} over the 1 chord in place of {{1}}.
